title: Open models have real benefits. Do they outweigh the risks?
key_facts: Late in September 2026, Anthropic released a report arguing that GLM-5.3, a model released in August by the Chinese company Z.ai and free to download and modify, poses a major cyberattack risk.
Closed models are more capable than open ones: the top eight on the Artificial Analysis leaderboard are all closed, though open models are only a handful of months behind.

Benefits of open models cited: researchers can study their inner workings, businesses can run them locally on sensitive data and they usually cost less, and they challenge the control of a few frontier labs.
Risks cited: open models have no filter checking prompts and no way to revoke access, and researchers have shown that safety training is easy to remove by retraining.
The article says closed models are also misused, citing Anthropic's risk report on hacking operations assisted by Claude and an autonomous hack by OpenAI agents against Hugging Face in July.

Proposed middle paths include training models that never learn about hacking, tamper-resistant models and staged release; no current tamper-resistance approach holds up against all attacks, according to a recent preprint.
The article notes Nvidia and Anthropic have commercial incentives on opposite sides of the debate.
quote_evidence: Late last month, Anthropic released a report arguing that the model GLM-5.3 poses a major cyberattack risk.
In practice, however, no current approaches to making models tamper-resistant hold up against all tampering attacks, according to a recent preprint.
But it would be a vast oversimplification to deem open models dangerous and closed models safe.
why_it_matters_hint: The debate shapes whether governments and labs restrict or promote freely downloadable AI models.
event_date: 13 Oct 2026 (explainer); the Anthropic report it refers to was "late last month"
notes: An explainer (analysis), not breaking news; its trigger, Anthropic's GLM-5.3 report, dates from late September 2026, but the piece itself is new on 13 Oct 2026, so freshness is NEW. Opinions are the experts' as quoted by MIT Technology Review.
